record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: What homogenized models describe acoustic phenomena in porous media and flows between two neighboring plates, including Hele-Shaw-type settings where integro-differential homogenized equations appear as they do in viscoelasticity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following two homogenization problems in continuum mechanics.

(A) Acoustics in a porous medium. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain occupied by a periodic two-phase composite at small scale $\varepsilon>0$: a connected elastic solid skeleton $\Omega^s_\varepsilon$ saturated by a viscous (or viscoelastic) fluid in the complementary pore network $\Omega^f_\varepsilon$, with $Y=Y^s\cup Y^f$ the unit periodicity cell. The displacement $u^s_\varepsilon$ in the solid satisfies the linear elasticity equations $\rho^s\partial_{tt}u^s_\varepsilon-\nabla\cdot(\mathbb{C}\,e(u^s_\varepsilon))=0$ in $\Omega^s_\varepsilon$, and the fluid velocity $v^f_\varepsilon$ and pressure $p^f_\varepsilon$ satisfy the (linearized) Navier–Stokes or Stokes system, with continuity of velocity and traction across the interface $\partial\Omega^s_\varepsilon\cap\partial\Omega^f_\varepsilon$. Determine, in a fully rigorous way (e.g., via two-scale convergence or periodic unfolding), the homogenized macroscopic system governing $(u^s,v^f,p^f)$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, in all relevant scaling regimes of viscosity, frequency, and contrast of constituents, and identify the precise structure (e.g., Biot-type elasticity with memory, or integro-differential constitutive laws arising from cell problems) of the limit equations.

(B) Hele-Shaw type flow between two close plates. Consider a viscous fluid filling a thin gap $\Omega_\varepsilon=\{(x,z):x\in\omega,\,0<z<\varepsilon h(x)\}$ between two nearly parallel plates with possibly rough/periodic gap profile $h$, governed by the Stokes (or Navier–Stokes) equations with no-slip on the plates. Derive the homogenized two-dimensional limit model on $\omega$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, including settings (variable gap, slip conditions, time-dependent boundaries, free boundary) where the resulting effective equation is an integro-differential equation in time of memory (viscoelastic-like) type, and characterize the memory kernel through appropriate cell problems.

Provide rigorous homogenized models for (A) and (B), state the precise hypotheses under which they hold, and clarify when an integro-differential (memory) structure necessarily appears in the limit.
artifact.category_tag: Homogenization of porous media and thin-film flows
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress exists: rigorous homogenization of fluid-structure interaction in porous media saturated by viscous or viscoelastic fluids (yielding Biot-type/integro-differential limit models) has been obtained via two-scale convergence and periodic unfolding, and homogenization of the Hele-Shaw problem in periodic and spatiotemporal media has been carried out, producing effective free boundary problems. However, many regimes (general scalings of viscosity/contrast, random or non-periodic geometries, nonlinear/free-boundary thin film flows, full characterization of memory kernels) remain open.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of the fluid–structure interaction in acoustics of porous media perfused by viscous fluid
status_evidence.snippet: Homogenization results of fluid–structure interaction in porous structures under quasi-static and dynamic loading regimes via periodic unfolding and asymptotic expansion, providing effective model parameters and macroscopic model.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous homogenized models for acoustics in viscous-fluid-saturated porous media have been derived.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of the Hele-Shaw Problem in Periodic Spatiotemporal Media
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions converge in the homogenization limit to a solution of a homogeneous Hele-Shaw-type problem with possibly nonlinear dependence of the free boundary velocity on the gradient.
status_evidence.claim: Homogenization of Hele-Shaw problems in periodic spatiotemporal media has been established.

status_evidence.title: A generalized macroscopic model for sound-absorbing poroelastic media
status_evidence.snippet: Acoustics of porous media saturated by incompressible viscous or viscoelastic fluid via homogenization, yielding biphasic, elastic, and viscoelastic behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Integro-differential (memory) effective equations arise in homogenized porous-media acoustics.
